qgdb1.intro: The Orthodox Queen's Gambit Declined. Black keeps the centre with c6 and Nbd7, and the rook comes to e8.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop. The light-squared bishop stays behind the chain for now.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and breaks that pin.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6. The c-pawn stays free to move.
Rc1 puts the rook on the c-file, behind the pawn on c4.
c6 supports the pawn on d5. This solid pawn is the Orthodox choice.
Qc2 develops the queen on the c-file and looks toward the centre.
Re8 puts the rook on the e-file, behind the pawn on e6.

qgdb2.intro: The freeing jump. Black takes on c4 and plants the knight on d5 against White's dark-squared bishop.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop. The light-squared bishop stays behind the chain for now.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and breaks that pin.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6. The c-pawn stays free to move.
Rc1 puts the rook on the c-file, behind the pawn on c4.
c6 supports the pawn on d5.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims toward the kingside.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4 and opens lines. This capture is how Black starts to free the position.
Bxc4 recaptures the pawn on c4 and keeps the light-squared bishop on an active diagonal.
Nd5 plants the knight in the centre and attacks the knight on c3. Black is ready to trade off White's active pieces.

qgdb3.intro: An early Exchange. White takes on d5 before developing the king's knight, and h3 gives the king air.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and fixes the central structure. This is the Exchange.
exd5 recaptures the pawn on d5 and opens the e-file. The light-squared bishop is no longer shut in.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and breaks that pin.
e3 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims toward the kingside.
c6 supports the pawn on d5.
h3 takes g4 away from Black's pieces and gives the king a flight square.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the centre.

qgdb4.intro: The Exchange with normal development. Both sides castle, the knight comes to d7, and the rook to e8.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5. The Exchange fixes the pawns before the minor pieces are all out.
exd5 recaptures the pawn on d5 and opens the e-file.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and breaks that pin.
e3 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims toward the kingside.
c6 supports the pawn on d5.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Re8 puts the rook on the half-open e-file.

qgdb5.intro: The Exchange with the knight on e2. The queen comes to c2, and Black's rook meets the half-open e-file.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and chooses the Exchange.
exd5 recaptures the pawn on d5 and opens the e-file.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and breaks that pin.
e3 supports the pawn on d4 and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims toward the kingside.
c6 supports the pawn on d5.
Qc2 develops the queen behind the bishop on d3. The two pieces share the diagonal toward the kingside.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight.
Nge2 develops the king's knight beside the centre. The f-pawn stays free.
Re8 puts the rook on the half-open e-file.

qgdb6.intro: Orthodox move order with Nf3 first. The dark-squared bishop comes to e7 before White pins, and the rook still lands on c1.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop. The light-squared bishop stays behind the chain for now.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and supports the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling. It will stand behind the knight if White pins.
Bg5 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the knight on f6. The bishop on e7 already stands between that knight and the queen.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6. The c-pawn stays free.
Rc1 puts the rook on the c-file, behind the pawn on c4.
c6 supports the pawn on d5. The Orthodox wall is complete.

qgdb7.intro: A quiet Queen's Gambit with Bd3. Black answers c5 and brings the knight to c6.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and prepares castling.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims toward the kingside.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and challenges the centre. Black does not stay cramped.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and adds pressure to the pawn on d4.

qgdb8.intro: The Ragozin. The bishop pins from b4, the queen recaptures on f6, and Black breaks with c5.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1. This pin is the Ragozin.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8. Both sides have a pin.
h6 asks the bishop on g5 a question before Black castles.
Bxf6 takes the knight on f6 rather than drop the bishop back.
Qxf6 recaptures the bishop on f6. The queen comes out and the pin on c3 remains.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Rc1 puts the rook on the c-file, behind the pawn on c4.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4 and opens the position for the queen.
Bxc4 recaptures the pawn on c4. The light-squared bishop takes up an active square.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4. Black strikes while the pin on c3 is still there.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king steps off the pin.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the centre.

qgdb9.intro: The Lasker Defence. Black asks the bishop a question, jumps the knight to e4, and then takes on c3.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and breaks that pin.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
h6 asks the bishop on g5 a question.
Bh4 keeps the dark-squared bishop on the diagonal and steps off the pawn.
Ne4 is the Lasker jump. The knight attacks the knight on c3 and starts the freeing trades.
Bxe7 takes the bishop on e7. White removes that bishop before the knight trade.
Qxe7 recaptures the bishop on e7 and develops the queen.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and attacks the knight on e4.
Nxc3 takes the knight on c3. Black carries out the trade the jump was aiming at.

qgdb10.intro: The Tartakower. After h6 and Bh4, Black fianchettos the light-squared bishop and develops the knight to d7.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5. This is the Queen's Gambit.
e6 supports the pawn on d5 and frees the dark-squared bishop. The light-squared bishop will need another route.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and breaks that pin.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
h6 asks the bishop on g5 a question.
Bh4 keeps the dark-squared bishop on the diagonal and steps off the pawn.
b6 prepares the fianchetto. The e-pawn shuts the light-squared bishop in, so Black develops it on the long diagonal.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims toward the kingside.
Bb7 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal. This is the Tartakower.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
